Unlike regular myopia (shortsightedness), progressive myopia worsens over time and leads to increasingly severe visual impairment. It often begins during childhood or adolescence and can continue into adulthood if left untreated. Asian ethnic children are disproportionately affected by progressive myopia. Studies show a higher prevalence in this population compared to the general population.
